title: Benchmark report: scope lock + success metrics (latency per $ across models/regions)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Public Benchmark Report: Latency per Dollar
description:
## Why
We are publishing a public-facing benchmark report focused on production economics: **latency per dollar** (with supporting throughput/cost metrics) by **model family** and **cloud region**.

This ticket defines the **scope + KPIs** and establishes the **acceptance criteria** for “ready to publish” (methodology defensibility, claims language, and launch readiness).

## Goals (what success looks like)
1) Establish Redwood as a credible reference for production-economics benchmarking (latency/$) with a transparent, reproducible methodology.
2) Drive qualified inbound for Hosted API and Dedicated/Private with clear CTAs and a follow-up motion.
3) Equip Sales/SE/Support with consistent talk tracks and a defensible methodology/claims FAQ.

## Primary KPIs (launch + 30 days)
### Funnel / demand
- **Report downloads:** 2,500 total downloads (landing page gated download) with >= 30% from net-new users.
- **Hosted API signups influenced:** 600 net-new signups attributed to benchmark campaign UTMs within 30 days.
- **Sales conversion:** 60 “book a consult” / demo requests from benchmark CTAs; 20 SQLs created with benchmark as primary source.
- **Pipeline influence:** $1.5M influenced pipeline (multi-touch) tagged to campaign within 60 days.

### Credibility / distribution
- **Analyst briefings completed:** 8 briefings; 3 follow-up requests for methodology or data tables.
- **Earned/social:** 150k total social impressions; 25 high-signal shares (engineers / infrastructure leaders) and >= 10 linkbacks.

### Quality gates (must-pass)
- Methodology + variance language signed off by Applied ML (Jonas/Claire) and SRE (Sean/Neha).
- External claims comply with performance-claims guidelines; no “best/fastest” absolute claims without context/CI.

## Scope (what we will publish)
### Workloads (public report)
We will benchmark two baseline workloads that reflect common production usage patterns and are reproducible:

1) **Chat / text generation (streaming)**
- Endpoint: chat completions (streaming on)
- Output length: fixed distribution (short/medium/long) to avoid cherry-picking
- Input length: mixed distribution representative of app traffic (short prompts + longer system/context)
- Concurrency levels: low/medium/high (exact values in internal methodology doc)
- Metrics shown publicly: p50/p95 end-to-end latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M output tokens, derived latency/$

2) **Embeddings**
- Endpoint: embeddings
- Input length distribution: short/medium/long
- Batch policy: fixed and disclosed
- Metrics shown publicly: p50/p95 latency, vectors/sec (or req/sec), cost per 1M tokens, derived latency/$

**Out of scope:** reranking, tool-calling-specific workloads, multimodal, fine-tuning, long-context “max window” stress tests.

### Regions (public report)
We will publish results for the following Redwood regions (with per-region tables and clear region labeling):
- **NA:** us-east (N. Virginia), us-west (Oregon)
- **EU:** eu-west (Ireland), eu-central (Frankfurt)
- **APAC:** ap-southeast (Singapore)

Notes:
- We will not generalize results across regions. All headline statements must include “in region X” or “across the regions tested.”
- If a region has constrained capacity during the benchmark window, results must be rerun or excluded (see variance + rerun policy).

### Models (public report)
We will publish a curated set of popular open(-weights) model families aligned with customer demand, plus at least one “efficiency” option:

**Chat / generation models** (final list locked by 2025-01-29):
- Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
- Llama 3.1 70B Instruct
- Mistral 7B Instruct (or current equivalent in catalog)
- Mixtral 8x7B Instruct
- Qwen2.5 7B Instruct
- Qwen2.5 72B Instruct
- Gemma 2 9B Instruct

**Embedding models**:
- bge-large-en (or current catalog equivalent)
- e5-large-v2 (or current catalog equivalent)
- bge-m3 (multilingual coverage)

Inclusion criteria:
- Available in Redwood catalog in all regions above (or explicitly marked “not available in region X”).
- Stable serving configuration during benchmark window (no mid-run runtime changes; see guardrails).
- Clear licensing posture appropriate for publication.

**Out of scope:** closed models, beta models without stable capacity, customer-specific fine-tunes.

## Metric definitions (public summary)
- **Latency**: end-to-end request latency measured at Redwood edge (includes queueing + runtime). p50 and p95.
- **Cost per 1M tokens**: derived from metering for the benchmark configuration (publicly presented as $/1M tokens).
- **Latency per dollar (latency/$)**: derived metric combining latency and cost to capture production economics. Exact computation will be disclosed in the methodology appendix.

Reporting rules:
- Provide variability notes (run-to-run variance summary); show confidence/variance bands where feasible.
- Do not present a single “winner” without qualifying workload + region context.

Target public launch window: **2025-02-26 (Wed)**

## Acceptance criteria (“Ready to publish” definition)
### Data + methodology
- [ ] Coverage matrix finalized (models x regions x workloads) with explicit exclusions.
- [ ] Benchmark runs completed for all in-scope combinations OR excluded combinations documented with reason.
- [ ] Variance analysis complete; reruns executed per policy; anomalies triaged and signed off (Perf/Evals).
- [ ] Cost attribution validated (metering + spot checks) and signed off (Nadia Rahman / Finance partner as needed).

### Claims + content
- [ ] Landing page + PDF report contain: methodology summary, limitations, and “how to interpret” section.
- [ ] Any comparative language follows external claims guidelines (no unqualified superlatives).
- [ ] Charts follow design system and have readable axes/units; accessibility checks complete.

### Security / privacy
- [ ] No customer data included; no raw per-request logs or identifiers published.
- [ ] Public tables sanitized and generated via deterministic pipeline; reviewed by Eng + Legal.

### Launch readiness
- [ ] Sales enablement package complete (deck + one-pager + competitive FAQ) and field training delivered.
- [ ] Support macros ready; escalation paths defined for methodology/variance questions.
- [ ] Tracking in place: UTMs, landing page events, download conversion, and dashboard for daily monitoring.

## Links / artifacts
- Methodology (internal): confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/.../latency-per-dollar-benchmark-methodology
- Claims guidelines (internal): confluence/architecture-and-standards/.../public-benchmarking-claims-guidelines
- Launch checklist: google_drive/.../launch-checklist-and-owners
- Table build pipeline: ENG-2872

## Open questions (resolved by scope lock date)
1) Do we include a small “repro harness” example at launch or follow-up week?
2) Embeddings: do we publish vectors/sec or req/sec as the primary throughput metric (to avoid confusion)?
3) Region naming: finalize canonical labels for site + API docs to prevent support tickets.

## Non-goals
- We are not trying to prove absolute superiority across all workloads.
- We are not publishing raw logs, traces, or per-request artifacts.
- We will not optimize runtime settings solely for the benchmark harness (guardrails required).
